Surah al-Anbiya' (The Prophets) [Meccan; it has 112 verses and was revealed after Surah Ibrahim]

﴿The reckoning of mankind has drawn near⁠﴾: it has come close. ﴿for the people⁠﴾: the people of Makkah who deny the resurrection. ﴿their reckoning⁠﴾: on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿yet they are heedless⁠﴾: of it, ﴿turning away⁠﴾: from preparing for it through faith.
﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, but it is newly revealed﴾ piece by piece, i.e., the wording of the Qur'an. ﴿Except that they listen to it while playing﴾ mocking.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 3:

﴿Heedless﴾ (lāhiyah), unaware, ﴿their hearts﴾ of its meaning. ﴿And they conspire in secret﴾ (wa-asarrū al-najwā), the speech. ﴿Those who did wrong﴾ (alladhīna ẓalamū) is a substitute (badal) for the wāw in ﴿they conspire﴾. ﴿Is this [Muhammad]﴾ (hal hādhā), i.e., Muhammad, ﴿anything but a human like you?﴾ So what he brings is sorcery. ﴿Will you then submit to sorcery?﴾ (afa-ta'tūna al-siḥr), follow it, ﴿while you see﴾ (wa-antum tubṣirūn), know that it is sorcery.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 4:

﴿He said﴾ to them: ﴿My Lord knows the word﴾ spoken ﴿in the heaven and the earth. And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of what they conceal, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of it.

"Bal" (بل) here marks a shift from one topic to another in all three places. ﴿They said﴾ concerning what he brought of the Qur'an: ﴿it is a jumble of dreams﴾, mixtures they saw in sleep. ﴿Rather, he has invented it﴾, fabricated it. ﴿Rather, he is a poet﴾, so what he brought is poetry. ﴿Let him then bring us a sign, as the earlier ones were sent﴾, like the she-camel, the staff and the hand.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 6:

﴿Before them, no town that We destroyed had believed.﴾ That is, its people; ﴿We destroyed them﴾ for denying the signs that came to them. ﴿Will they then believe?﴾ No.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 7:

﴿And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed⦆ — and in another reading, with the yāʾ and a fatḥah on the ḥāʾ (nūḥī becoming yūḥā) — ﴿to them﴾, [namely] the angels. ﴿So ask the people of the reminder﴾, [namely] the scholars of the Torah and the Gospel, ﴿if you do not know﴾ that. For they know it, and you are closer to accepting their testimony than the believers are to accepting [the testimony] of Muhammad.
﴿And We did not make them﴾, i.e., the messengers, ﴿bodies﴾, meaning bodies (in the plural), ﴿that do not eat food﴾, but rather they eat it. ﴿Nor were they immortal﴾ in the world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 9:

﴿Then We fulfilled the promise to them﴾ by saving them, ﴿and We saved them, and whom We willed﴾ of those who believed in them, ﴿and We destroyed the transgressors﴾ those who denied them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 10:

﴿Indeed We have sent down to you﴾ O assembly of Quraysh, ﴿a Book in which is your mention﴾ because it is in your language, ﴿Then will you not reason?﴾ so that you believe in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 11:

﴿And how many a town did We shatter﴾ (We destroyed) ﴿from a town﴾ (i.e., its people) ﴿which was wrongdoing﴾ (disbelieving)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 12:

﴿When they sensed Our might﴾: the people of the town perceived the destruction, ﴿behold, they were fleeing from it﴾: running away quickly.

Then the angels said to them, mockingly: ﴿Do not flee, and return to what you were made to enjoy of luxury therein, and to your dwellings, that perhaps you may be questioned﴾ [i.e., about some of your worldly affairs, as is customary].
They said, "Woe to us!" (the particle "yā" is for alerting), "Indeed we were wrongdoers" in disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 15:

﴿Their cry continued﴾ (fa-ma zalat tilka) the words, ﴿their cry﴾ (da'wahum). They kept calling out with them and repeating them, ﴿until We made them as a harvest﴾ (hasidan) like the crop cut down with sickles, by being killed with the sword, ﴿extinguished﴾ (khamidin), dead, like the dying out of a fire when it goes out.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 16:

﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play.﴾ Playing, i.e., without purpose, but rather as signs pointing to Our power and benefiting Our servants.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 17:

﴿If We had intended to take a pastime,﴾ [something to amuse oneself with, such as a wife or a child], ﴿We would have taken it from Our presence,﴾ [from what is with Us], [of the large-eyed maidens (ḥūr 'īn) and the angels], ﴿if We were ever to do [so].﴾ [That is, had We done it], but We did not do it, so We did not intend it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 21, verse 18:

﴿Nay, We hurl the truth﴾ (narmi, "We cast") ﴿against falsehood﴾ — i.e., the faith (al-iman) against disbelief (al-kufr) — ﴿so it crushes it﴾ (yudhhibuhu, "removes it"), ﴿and behold, it vanishes﴾ (dhahiq, "departing"). The verb damagha originally means: he struck his brain with a blow, and that is a fatal wound. ﴿And woe to you﴾ (al-wayl, "the severe punishment") ﴿for what you describe﴾ — O disbelievers of Makkah — ﴿of God﴾, of wives and children.

[To Him belongs] ﴿whoever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ as dominion, ﴿and whoever is with Him﴾, meaning the angels, is a مُبْتَدَأ (mubtada', the subject of a nominal sentence) whose خَبَر (khabar, the predicate) is ﴿do not disdain to worship Him, nor do they grow weary﴾, meaning they do not tire.
﴿They glorify Him night and day; they never slacken﴾ in it, so it is for them like breath is for us: nothing preoccupies us from it.

Or have they taken gods from the earth, [gods] that raise the dead?

(Here) "am" is in the sense of "bal" (rather), for transition, and the hamza is for denial. "Ittakhadhu" (have they taken): "alihah" (gods) existing "min al-ard" (from the earth), like a stone, gold and silver. "Hum" (they), i.e., the gods, "yanshurun" (raise), i.e., give life to the dead? No. And none is a god except one who gives life to the dead.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 22:

﴿Had there been in them﴾ i.e., in the heavens and the earth, ﴿gods other than Allah﴾ i.e., other than Him, ﴿they would have been corrupted﴾ i.e., they would have gone out of their ordered arrangement which is observed, because of the existence of mutual opposition between them, in accordance with the customary practice when there are multiple rulers: opposition regarding a matter and failure to agree upon it. ﴿Glory be to Allah﴾, a declaration of His transcendence, ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾, the Creator of the Throne, i.e., the Kursi, ﴿above what they describe﴾, the unbelievers describe Allah with, of partners to Him and other things.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 23:

﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.﴾ (They will be questioned) about their actions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 24:

﴿Or have they taken gods besides Him?﴾ (Exalted is He) — that is, other than Him. The interrogative here is one of rebuke. ﴿Say: Bring your proof﴾ for that, and there is no way to it. ﴿This is the reminder of those with me﴾, my community, and it is the Qur'an. ﴿And the reminder of those before me﴾ from the nations, and it is the Torah, the Gospel, and other books of God, none of which contains that there is a god with God, from what they claim. Exalted is He above that. ﴿Rather, most of them do not know the truth﴾, the Oneness of God, ﴿so they are turning away﴾ from the reflection that leads to it.

﴿We did not send any messenger before you except that We revealed to him that there is no god but Me, so worship Me.﴾ In another recitation, it is read with the letter ياء (ya') and a fatha on the letter حاء (ha'), so that the verb is passive. Meaning: declare Me to be One (tawhid, affirming the oneness of God).
And they say, "﴿The Most Merciful has taken a son﴾," referring to the angels. ﴿Glory be to Him!﴾ ﴿Rather,﴾ they are ﴿honored servants﴾ with Him, and servitude is incompatible with begetting.
﴿They do not speak before Him in speech﴾: they do not utter their own words except after His word. ﴿And they act by His command﴾: i.e., after it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 28:

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾, i.e., what they have done and what they will do. ﴿And they cannot intercede except for him whom He approves﴾, i.e., whom He wishes to intercede for. ﴿And they are apprehensive of His fear﴾, i.e., of God, ﴿apprehensive﴾, fearful.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 29:

﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him"﴾ — i.e., besides Allah, meaning other than Him; and this is Iblis, who called people to worship himself and commanded them to obey him. ﴿That is how We will recompense him: Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ — the polytheists, just as We recompense him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 21, verse 30:

﴿Awa-lam﴾ (with a waw, and without it) ﴿yara﴾ (i.e., ya'lam, "know") ﴿alladhina kafaru anna as-samawati wal-ard kanata ratqan﴾ (closed, i.e., ratq here means sadd, in the sense of maftuqa... "mas'udah," meaning closed-up/sealed) ﴿fa-fatqnahuma﴾ (We made the heaven seven and the earth seven; or, He split the heaven by sending rain when it did not rain, and split the earth by making it bring forth plants when it did not bring them forth) ﴿wa-ja'alna min al-ma'\u2019\u00a0 an-nazil min as-sama'\u2019 wan-na bi' min al-ard﴾ (the water that descends from the sky and springs from the earth) ﴿kulla shay'in hayy﴾ (every living thing, of plants and other things; i.e., water is the cause of their life) ﴿afala yu'minun﴾ (in My Oneness)

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 31:

﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains﴾, meaning fixed mountains, ﴿lest﴾ (أنْ) it ﴿shake﴾, meaning move, ﴿with them﴾. ﴿And We placed in it﴾, meaning in the earth, the mountains ﴿broad roads﴾, meaning passages, ﴿roads﴾ (سُبُلًا) is a substitute (badal) for ﴿paths﴾ (طُرُقًا), meaning wide, open, passable ways, ﴿so that they may be guided﴾, meaning to their destinations in their journeys.

"And We made the sky a roof, protected," for the earth, as a roof is for a house, "[protected]" from falling. "Yet they, from its signs," the sun, the moon and the stars, "turn away," not reflecting upon them, so that they would know that their Creator has no partner.

The commentary here concerns the tanwin in كُلّ (kull). Its tanwin is a substitute (ʿiwaḍ) for the genitive noun that was omitted, namely "the sun and the moon," and it also covers what follows, which is "the stars" (al-nujūm). ﴿In an orbit﴾ that is circular, like the millstone in the sky. ﴿They swim﴾, that is, they move swiftly, like a swimmer in water. The plural pronoun denoting rational beings (ḍamīr jamʿ man yaʿqil) is used because of the comparison to swimmers.

It was revealed when the disbelievers said, "Muhammad will die": ﴿We did not grant to any human before you eternity﴾ (al-khuld), i.e., remaining in the world; ﴿so if you die, will they be the ones who remain (al-khalidun)﴾ in it? No. The last clause is the place of the interrogative of denial (al-istifham al-inkari).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 35:

﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ in this world. ﴿And We test you﴾ (nakhtabirukum, We try you) ﴿with evil and with good﴾ such as poverty and wealth, sickness and health, ﴿as a trial﴾ (fitnah), which is a maf'ul lahu (object of purpose, i.e., a verbal complement of reason), meaning: so that We may see whether you will be patient and thankful or not. ﴿And to Us you will be returned﴾, so We will recompense you.

﴿When those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in mockery﴾, i.e., one who is mocked at. They say, ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾, i.e., disparages them, ﴿while they are disbelievers in the Most Merciful when it is mentioned to them﴾. ﴿They﴾ is an emphasis (ta'kid), ﴿disbelievers﴾ in Him, since they said, "We do not know Him."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 37:

It was revealed concerning their hastiness for the punishment: ﴿Man was created of haste.﴾ That is, because of his great hastiness in his affairs, it is as if he was created from it. ﴿I will show you My signs﴾, that is, My promises of punishment. ﴿So do not ask Me to hasten it﴾, meaning, so He showed them the killing at Badr.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 38:

﴿And they say, "When is this promise," of the Resurrection, "if you are truthful" about it?﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 39:

﴿If only those who disbelieved would know the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, and they will not be helped.﴾ (yadfa'una) they will not be able to push away (ʿan wujuhihim al-nar) the Fire from their faces, (wa la ʿan zuhurihim) nor from their backs, (wa la hum yunsaruna) and they will not be helped; (yumna'una minha) they will not be prevented from it on the Day of Resurrection. (Wa jawab law ma qalu dhalika) The answer to "law" (if only) is: they did not say that (i.e., they did not say this when they were in the world).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 40:

﴿Nay, but it will come upon them suddenly﴾, the Resurrection, ﴿and confound them﴾, bewilder them, ﴿so they will not be able to avert it, nor will they be reprieved﴾, given time for repentance or excuse.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 41:

﴿And indeed, messengers before you were mocked﴾. In this there is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿So there befell﴾, i.e., descended, ﴿those who mocked among them that which they used to mock﴾, namely the punishment. Thus it likewise befalls those who mock you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 42:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Who will protect you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?﴾ That is, from His punishment, should it descend upon you. Meaning: no one does so. And those addressed do not fear God's punishment, because of their denial of it. ﴿Nay, they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿refusing﴾ to reflect upon it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 43:

﴿Am﴾ (or) here carries the meaning of the interrogative hamza, for denunciation. ﴿Do they have gods that protect them﴾ from what displeases them ﴿apart from Us?﴾ That is: do they have anyone other than Us who protects them from it? No! ﴿They are unable to help themselves﴾ meaning the gods are unable to help themselves, so they cannot help them ﴿nor will they be accompanied﴾ meaning the disbelievers will not be protected ﴿from Us﴾ from Our punishment ﴿yuṣḥabūn﴾ (they will be given protection). It is said: ṣaḥibaka Allāh, meaning: may God guard you and grant you protection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 44:

﴿Nay, We gave enjoyment to these and their fathers﴾ with the blessings We bestowed upon them, ﴿until a long life passed over them﴾ so they became deluded by that. ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land﴾ intending their land, ﴿reducing it from its extremities﴾ by the conquest [granted] to the Prophet. ﴿Are they then the victors?﴾ No, rather the Prophet and his Companions are.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 21, verse 45:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿I only warn you by the revelation﴾ from God, not from my own self. ﴿But the deaf do not hear the call when﴾ they ﴿are warned﴾, (the two hamzas are pronounced as they stand, with the second softened to a sound between itself and the yaa'), because they do not act on what they have heard of the warning, so they are like the deaf.

And if a breath of your Lord's punishment should touch them, [meaning] a light blow, they would surely say: "Alas for us! (Yā for alerting attention) Ruin for us! Indeed we were wrongdoers," through associating partners [with God] and denying Muhammad (ﷺ).

We set up the scales of justice (ذَوات العَدْل, i.e. possessing justice) for the Day of Resurrection (أيْ فِيهِ, i.e. in it), so that no soul will be wronged in the least: no reduction of a good deed or addition to a bad deed. Even if the deed is the weight of a grain of mustard seed (مِثْقال زِنَة حَبَّة مِن خَرْدَل), We will bring it (أتَيْنا بِها, i.e. with its weight). And We suffice as Reckoners (مُحْصِينَ كُلّ شَيْء, i.e. counting every thing).
We gave Musa and Harun the Furqan, meaning the Torah, which distinguishes between truth and falsehood and between the lawful and the unlawful. And a light, by it, and a reminder, an admonition by it.
Those who fear their Lord in the unseen (bil-ghayb), meaning: away from people, in private, [when] they are unseen by them, ﴿and they, of the Hour﴾, meaning its terrors, ﴿are apprehensive﴾, fearful.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 50:

﴿And this﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is a blessed reminder which We have sent down. Will you then deny it?﴾ The interrogation (al-istifham) in it is for rebuke (al-tawbikh).

And We certainly gave Ibrahim his rectitude before (this), and We were knowing of him [as being fit for it]. (Tafsir al-Jalalayn: "his rectitude" means He guided him before he reached maturity, i.e., before his puberty; "knowing of him" means knowing that he was worthy of that.)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 52:

﴿When he said to his father and his people: "What are these statues to which you are devoted?"﴾ The idols. ﴿To which you are devoted﴾ i.e., persisting in worshipping them.
﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them, so we followed in their footsteps."﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 54:

[He] said [to them], ﴿Indeed you were, you and your fathers﴾ [in worshipping them], ﴿in clear error﴾ [manifest].
They said, "Have you come to us with the truth in what you say, or are you among the players (in jest)?" — i.e., in this statement of yours.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 56:

﴿He said: Rather, your Lord﴾ the one deserving of worship, ﴿is the Lord﴾ the owner of ﴿the heavens and the earth, who originated them﴾ created them without any precedent model, ﴿and I am of those who bear witness﴾ to ﴿that﴾ which I have said.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 21, verse 58:

﴿So he made them﴾ (after they had gone off to their gathering on a day of festival for them) ﴿into fragments (judhadhan)﴾ (with the jim vowelled either with a damma or a kasra): crumbs, with an axe, ﴿except for the biggest of them﴾ (for them; he hung the axe around its neck), ﴿so that they might return to it﴾ (i.e., to the biggest) ﴿and see what he had done to the others﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 21, verse 59:

﴿They said﴾ after their return and seeing what had been done: ﴿"Who has done this to our gods? Surely he is among the wrongdoers."﴾ Therein (fihi) is the sense of…
﴿They said﴾, i.e., some of them to others, ﴿"We heard a youth mention them"﴾, i.e., disparaging them.
They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people," that is, openly, "so that they may bear witness" against him that he is the one who did it.

﴿They said﴾ to him after his coming, ﴿"Are you"﴾ [أأَنْتَ], with the two hamzahs pronounced in full (تَحْقِيق, *tahqiq*, the full articulation of a hamza), the second hamzah changed to an alif, eased (تَسْهِيل, *tashil*, softening the hamza), an alif inserted between the eased hamzah and the other one, and that alif omitted.

﴿He said﴾, refraining from mentioning his own act: ﴿"Rather, this one, their chief, did it. So ask them"﴾ about its doer ﴿"if they are able to speak."﴾ In it there is *taqdim jawab al-shart* (the placing of the response of the conditional before the condition), and in what precedes it there is *ta'rid* (an indirect allusion) to them, that an idol whose inability to act is known cannot be a god.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 64:

﴿So they returned to themselves﴾ through reflection, ﴿and said﴾ to themselves, ﴿"Indeed, you are the wrongdoers"﴾ in worshipping that which does not speak.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 65:

﴿Then they were turned back upon their heads﴾ from Allah, i.e., they were returned to their disbelief, and they said, "By Allah, you know that these do not speak," i.e., how then can you command us to ask them?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 66:

﴿He said: "Do you then worship, instead of Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ i.e., in place of Him, ﴿that which can neither benefit you at all﴾ with provision or anything else, ﴿nor harm you﴾ at all, if you do not worship Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 67:

﴿Uff﴾ with the fa' pronounced with a kasra or a fatha, as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning stench and ugliness, ﴿to you and to what you worship besides Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ that these idols do not deserve worship and are not fit for it, and that only Allah Most High deserves it.

They said, "Burn him," meaning Ibrahim, "and support your gods," meaning by burning him, "if you are going to act," [i.e., to support them].

So they gathered a great quantity of firewood, set fire to all of it, bound Ibrahim, placed him in a catapult, and hurled him into the fire.

We said: "O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim." So it did not burn anything of him except his bonds, its heat went away, and its light remained. And by His saying "and safety," he was preserved from death through its coolness.
﴿And they intended a scheme against him﴾, which was the burning, ﴿so We made them the greatest losers﴾ in what they intended.

And We delivered him and Lot, [Lot being] the son of his brother Haran, from Iraq, ﴿to the land which We had blessed for all the worlds﴾ with its abundance of rivers and trees, and it is ash-Sham (Syria). Ibrahim settled in Filastin (Palestine), and Lot in al-Mu'tafikah, and between them is a day's journey.

﴿And We bestowed upon him﴾, i.e., upon Ibrahim, who had asked for a child, as mentioned in [the surah of] al-Saffat, ﴿Isaac and Jacob as an extra gift﴾, i.e., an addition to what he had asked for. Or it means the son's son (grandson). ﴿And each of them﴾, i.e., he and his two sons, ﴿We made righteous﴾, i.e., prophets.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 21, verse 73:

﴿And We made them imams﴾ with the two hamzas pronounced as full hamzas (tahqiq, "verification" or "full articulation") and the second changed to a yā' (ibdal, "substitution"), that they might be followed in goodness. ﴿guiding﴾ people "by Our command" ﴿to Our religion﴾ "and We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of the prayer, and the giving of zakat." ﴿That is, that they be done, established, and given by them and by their followers.﴾ The hā' of إقامة (iqāmah) was deleted for lightness (takhfīf).

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** (the concise commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 21, verse 74:

﴿And to Lot We gave judgement (ḥukm), meaning a decisive ruling between the disputants, and knowledge, and We delivered him from the town that used to commit the foul deeds﴾, meaning its people used to do the abominable acts, ﴿of sodomy, and throwing pebbles (al-bunduq), and playing with birds, and other than that﴾. ﴿Indeed they were a people of evil﴾: an infinitive from sāʾahu, the opposite of sarrahu (it grieved him, the opposite of it pleased him).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 75:

﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy﴾ by saving him from his people.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 76:

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿Noah﴾, and what follows is a *badal* (substitution, i.e., an apposition) for it: ﴿when he called out﴾, meaning he invoked (a curse) against his people by his saying: ﴿"My Lord, do not leave"﴾ etc., ﴿before﴾, meaning before Abraham and Lot. ﴿So We answered him and saved him and his family﴾, those who were in his ship, ﴿from the great distress﴾, meaning the drowning and his people's denial of him.

And We helped him (ونصرناه) — We protected him (مَنَعْناه) — from the people who denied Our signs (بِآياتِنا), which indicated his prophethood (الدّالَّة عَلى رِسالَته), so that they could not reach him with harm.

And [mention] Dawud (David) and Sulayman (Solomon), that is, their story, and it may be read as a substitution for them both, when they judged concerning the tilth, which was a field of crops or a vineyard, when the sheep of the people strayed into it and grazed on it by night without a shepherd, having broken loose. And We were witness to their judgment. Here the plural pronoun is used for two persons. Dawud ruled that the owner of the tilth should take the sheep as compensation, and Sulayman said that the owner should benefit from their milk, their offspring and their wool until the tilth returns to what it was, by the owner's restoration of it, whereupon he returns the sheep to him.

﴿So We gave understanding of the matter﴾ (i.e., the judgment) ﴿to Sulayman﴾, and each of them We gave judgment and knowledge. The judgment and its ruling were by ijtihad (independent reasoning), and Dawud returned to Sulayman's ruling. It is also said that it was by revelation, and the second (ruling) abrogates the first (naskh).

﴿And to each﴾ of them ﴿We gave﴾ (ataynahu) ﴿judgment﴾, meaning prophethood, ﴿and knowledge﴾ of the matters of religion. ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Us] along with Dawud, and the birds﴾: likewise, they were made subservient to glorifying [Allah] along with him, by His command to him, whenever he found himself in a state of lassitude, so that he might be invigorated by it. ﴿And We were ever doers﴾ of the subjugation of their glorification along with him, even though it was a wonder in your eyes: that is, their responding to the Master Dawud.

Qur'anic quotations, transliterations and glosses follow the instructions. Here is the translation:

﴿And We taught him the making of chain-mail﴾: that is the coat of mail (dir', al-dir' — armour), because it is worn (tulbas), and he was the first to make it, and before it there were only plates. ﴿For you﴾ among the people, ﴿so that it may protect you﴾ with the letter nun (for God), and with the letter ya' (for Dawud), and with the letter ta' (for the lubus, i.e. the chain-mail), ﴿from your violence﴾: your war with your enemies. ﴿So will you﴾, O people of Makkah, ﴿be grateful﴾ for My blessings by believing in the Messenger? That is: give thanks to Me for that.

And to Solomon (We subjected) the wind, violently blowing, and in another verse, gently (rakhaa), meaning: strong in its blowing and gentle as he willed. It runs by his command to the land which We had blessed, namely the Levant (al-Sham), "and We have knowledge of all things." By this, God Most High knew that what He gave Solomon would lead him to submit to his Lord, so He did it in accordance with His knowledge.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 21, verse 82:

﴿And﴾ ﴿of the devils were those who dived for him,﴾ entering the sea and bringing forth from it pearls for Sulayman. ﴿And they performed other work besides that,﴾ i.e., other than diving, such as construction and other things. ﴿And We were guardians over them,﴾ lest they corrupt what they had done, because whenever they finished a task before nightfall, they would spoil it unless they were occupied with something else.

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿Ayyub﴾ (Job). It is in apposition (badal) to him: ﴿when he called out to his Lord﴾ after he was tried by the loss of all his wealth and children, the wasting of his body, the shunning of him by all the people except his wife, for three, seven, or eighteen years, and the hardship of his livelihood, saying: ﴿that adversity has touched me﴾. The word أنّي is read with the hamza vowelled with a fatha (بِفَتْحِ الهَمْزَة), with the preposition بِ (bi) understood before it, i.e. as بِأنّي. ﴿Adversity﴾ means hardship (الشِّدَّة, al-shiddah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 84:

﴿So We answered him﴾ his call, ﴿and removed what afflicted him of harm, and We gave him his family﴾ his children, both males and females, by bringing them back to life for him, and each of the two categories was three or seven, ﴿and the like thereof with them﴾ from his wife, and her youth was restored. He had a threshing floor for wheat and a threshing floor for barley, so God sent two clouds: one of them poured gold over the wheat threshing floor, and the other poured silver over the barley threshing floor, until it overflowed. ﴿A mercy﴾ is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), ﴿from Us﴾ is a qualifier, ﴿and a reminder for the worshippers﴾ so that they would be patient and thus be rewarded.
And Ismail, Idris and Dhul-Kifl: all of them were among the patient, (patient) in obedience to God and in refraining from His disobedience.

And We admitted them into Our mercy (from prophethood). Indeed they were among the righteous (who merit it). Dhul-Kifl was so named because he undertook (takaffala) to fast the whole of his day, to stand in prayer the whole of his night, to judge between people, and not to become angry; and he fulfilled all of that. It was also said that he was not a prophet.

"And [mention] Dhu'l-Nun (the Man of the Fish), who is Yunus ibn Matta (Yunus, son of Matta), and it is substituted for him, when he went off in anger (mughadiban) at his people, meaning angry with them because of what he had suffered from them, and he had not been permitted to do so. So he thought that We would not have power over him, meaning that We would not decree against him by what We had decreed concerning his imprisonment in the belly of the fish, or that We would constrict him by that. Then he cried out in the darknesses: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the belly of the fish, that there is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers, in my going away from among my people without permission."

So We answered him and delivered him from distress, ﴿So We responded to him and delivered him from the distress﴾ by means of those words. ﴿And thus﴾ just as We delivered him, ﴿We deliver the believers﴾ from their distress when they call upon Us in supplication.

And mention Zakariyya (Zechariah), which is substituted for the preceding (idh nada rabbahu), when he called upon his Lord, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave me alone (fardan)﴾, i.e., without a child to inherit from me, ﴿and You are the best of inheritors﴾, the One who remains after the annihilation of Your creation.

So We answered him, ﴿and We granted him Yahya (John)﴾ as a son, ﴿and We made his wife fit for him﴾, so that she bore the child after her barrenness. ﴿Indeed they﴾, that is, those prophets mentioned, ﴿used to hasten﴾ (yusari'una), i.e., hurry, ﴿to good deeds﴾ (al-khayrat), i.e., acts of obedience, ﴿and they called upon Us in hope﴾ (raghaban) of Our mercy ﴿and in fear﴾ (rahaban) of Our punishment. ﴿And they were humble before Us﴾ (khashi'in), i.e., humbly submissive in their worship.

And mention Mary, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit (i.e., Jibril (Gabriel), who blew into the opening of her garment, and so she conceived Jesus), and We made her and her son a sign for all the worlds (mankind, jinn and angels), in that she bore him without a male.

﴿Indeed, this﴾, i.e., the religion of Islam, ﴿is your community﴾, your religion, O you who are addressed; i.e., you must adhere to it. ﴿One community﴾ is a necessary circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl lāzimah, a state that cannot be separated from its subject). ﴿And I am your Lord, so worship Me﴾, i.e., affirm My oneness (waḥḥidūnī).

﴿And they divided﴾, i.e., some of those addressed, ﴿their affair among themselves﴾, i.e., they split the matter of their religion, differing over it. They are the sects of the Jews and the Christians. ﴿All to Us will they return﴾, i.e., We will recompense each one for his deed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 94:

﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, there will be no denial of his effort﴾, i.e., no rejection, ﴿and indeed, We are recording it for him﴾, by commanding the guardian angels to write it down, so that We reward him for it.

And it is forbidden upon a town which We have destroyed (that its people should not return)—meaning its people—that they do not return (the "lā" here is extra/redundant), i.e., their return to the world is impossible.

"Until" marks the limit of the impossibility of their returning, ﴿when it is opened﴾, read with lightening and doubling (بِالتَّخْفِيفِ والتَّشْدِيد), namely فُتِحَتْ (futiḥat). ﴿Yajuj and Majuj﴾, read with the hamza and without it (بِالهَمْزِ وتَرْكه), i.e., يَأْجُوج ومَأْجُوج (Ya'juj wa Ma'juj), are two non-Arabic names of two tribes. A noun governed by the phrase is to be understood before them, namely سَدّ (sadd, "barrier"), meaning "their barrier," i.e., sadduhuma. That refers to the approach of the Hour. ﴿And they will come from every mound﴾, meaning a raised place on the earth, ﴿swarming﴾, meaning they hasten.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 97:

﴿And the true promise draws near﴾, i.e., the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring fixedly﴾, i.e., the matter [will be such that]; on that Day, because of its severity, they will say: ﴿O woe to us!﴾ [the "yā" is for alerting], meaning: destruction to us. ﴿We were indeed in heedlessness of this﴾ in the world, ﴿Nay, we were wrongdoers﴾ to ourselves by our denial of the Messengers.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 21, verse 98:

﴿Indeed, you﴾ O people of Makkah, ﴿and what you worship besides Allah﴾ i.e., other than Him, of the idols, ﴿are fuel (ḥaṣab) for Hell﴾ its kindling, ﴿you will enter it﴾ i.e., you will enter into it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 99:

﴿If these﴾ idols ﴿were gods, as you claimed, they would not have entered it (hell)﴾, and all ﴿of them﴾, of the worshippers and the worshipped, ﴿will abide therein﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 100:

﴿For them﴾ (i.e., for the worshippers), ﴿therein is a roaring, and they therein will not hear﴾ anything, because of the intensity of its boiling. And it was revealed when Ibn al-Za'bara said: "Worshipping ʿUzayr, the Messiah and the angels," so they are in the Fire according to what has preceded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 101:

﴿Indeed, those for whom the good reward has preceded from Us﴾ the rank ﴿the best [reward]﴾, and among them are those who were mentioned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 102:

﴿They shall not hear its faint sound﴾, i.e., its noise, ﴿and they will abide in that which their souls desire﴾ of delight.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 103:

﴿Not will grieve them the greatest terror﴾, which is when the servant is commanded to the Fire. ﴿And the angels will receive them﴾, meeting them ﴿when they come forth from the graves﴾, saying to them: ﴿This is your Day which you were promised﴾ in the worldly life.

The Day [We shall fold up the heaven like the folding of the scroll for writings]. "Yawm" (the Day) is in the accusative, governed by a verb implied before it, meaning "mention" (dhukira muqaddaran). "We shall fold up the heaven like the folding of the scroll." "Al-sijill" is the name of an angel. "For writings": the "scroll" (ṣaḥīfa) of the son of Adam at the time of his death. The lam is extra (zā'ida), or "al-sijill" means the scroll, and "al-kitāb" in the sense of "the written", and the lam is in the sense of "ʿalā" (upon). In another reading, "lil-kutub" is in the plural.

[As We began the first creation], from non-existence, [so We shall return it], after its annihilation. So the kaf is connected to "nuʿīduhu" (We shall return it), its pronoun refers back to "awwal" (first), and "mā" is a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyya).

[A promise upon Us]: accusative, governed by an implied verb "waʿadnā" (We promised) before it, and it is an emphasis of the meaning of what precedes it. [Indeed We are ever doing] what We have promised.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 105:

﴿And We have certainly written in the Zabur﴾ meaning the Book, i.e., the revealed Books of Allah, ﴿after the Reminder﴾ meaning the Mother of the Book that is with Allah, ﴿that the earth﴾ the earth of Paradise, ﴿will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ a general statement covering every righteous person.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 106:

﴿Indeed, in this﴾ (the Qur'an) ﴿is surely a message﴾ (balaghan), meaning sufficiency for entering Paradise, ﴿for a people who worship﴾ (ʿābidīn), meaning those who act upon it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 107:

﴿And We did not send you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿except as a mercy﴾, i.e., as a mercy, ﴿to the worlds﴾, the humankind and the jinn, through you.

Say: ﴿Indeed, it is only revealed to me that your God is one God.﴾ That is, what is revealed to me concerning the matter of God is only His oneness (wahdaniyya, the state of being one). ﴿So will you submit?﴾ That is, will you be submissive to what is revealed to me of the oneness of God? The interrogative (istifham, a question form) here carries the sense of a command.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 109:

﴿But if they turn away﴾ from that, ﴿then say: I have announced to you﴾ I have informed you of the war, ﴿on equal terms﴾ a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to both the subject and the object, meaning: on equal footing in knowledge, so that I do not withhold it from you, in order that you may prepare yourselves. ﴿And I do not know whether﴾ (in) ﴿what you are promised is near or far﴾ of the punishment, or the Resurrection which includes it. Only Allah knows it.
﴿Indeed He﴾ (Exalted is He) ﴿knows what is spoken aloud﴾ of speech and deeds, from you and from others, ﴿and knows what you conceal﴾, you and others, of what is secret.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 111:

﴿And I do not know﴾ (i.e., I do not know) ﴿perhaps it is﴾ (i.e., I have not informed you of it, and its time has not been made known) ﴿a trial﴾ (i.e., a test) ﴿for you﴾ (so that it may be seen how you act) ﴿and an enjoyment﴾ (i.e., a provision) ﴿for a time﴾ (i.e., until the end of your lifespans). This is opposed to the first, which is expressed with "perhaps" (la'alla), whereas the second is not a place for hoping (taraji).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 21, verse 112:

﴿Say﴾ (and in one recitation: he said), ﴿"My Lord, judge﴾ between me and those who deny ﴿with truth"﴾, meaning, with the punishment upon them, or with victory over them. So they were punished at Badr, Uhud, Hunayn, al-Ahzab (the Confederates) and al-Khandaq (the Trench), and he was given victory over them. ﴿"And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the One whose help is sought against what you describe"﴾, meaning, against your lies about Allah in your saying ﴿"He has taken a son"﴾, and against me in your saying, "he is a sorcerer," and against the Qur'an in your saying, "it is poetry."
